name: Nakijin dialect of Northern Ryukyuan Japanese
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 1 other work consulted does not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Lawrence, Wayne P. (2011). More on Pitch, Stress, and Vowel Reduction [高さ，強勢および母音弱化再考]. Gengo Kenkyu (言語研究) 139: 111–119. doi:10.11435/gengo.139.0_111 (J-STAGE open PDF; saved)
catalog_locator: §3 'Aspiration Alternations without Stress', p. 115, second paragraph and fn. 9; abstract p. 111
catalog_quote: The Nakijin dialect of Northern Ryukyuan Japanese (Nakasone 1983) is a pitch accent language with an iambic foot structure. Stress plays no role in the phonology. Accents are assigned cyclically to either the penultimate mora (the unmarked case) or the ultimate mora (the marked case).9 High tones are assigned to the rightmost accent in a word, and also to the leftmost mora (the marked case) or first mora after the leftmost foot (the unmarked case) of a word. This High tone is then moved to the head of the foot it is in. All moras dominated by or located between High tones within a word are pronounced on a High pitch. ... Quantity-sensitive iambic feet are erected from left to right across words, prior to most compounding, and iambic lengthening generally applies, but is blocked on high vowels if adjacent to an accented mora. The foot structure is involved in a number of segmental processes (vowel lengthening, r-deletion, progressive palatalization), but is independent of accent position. [fn. 9] This account is simplified. There are words with no accent, due to other factors. Unaccented words are pronounced with a High tone on the ultimate mora. For a full account of the accentuation of the Nakijin dialect, the reader is referred to Lawrence (1990). [abstract, p. 111] In the Ryukyuan language of Nakijin, a pitch accent language with no phonemic stress, aspiration correlates with foot structure, not stress.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Kunigami (Nakijin/Yonamine dialect) has no stress; it is a lexical pitch accent language built on quantity-sensitive iambic feet. Each morpheme carries at most one accent, on the penultimate mora (default) or final mora (marked); high pitch spans from a rise after the initial foot (or from the first mora) up to the rightmost accent, and the accent also blocks iambic lengthening of adjacent high vowels. Descriptively (Ogawa 2012:41; Sakimura 1984:19; Curry 2004:36) nouns fall into three surface classes: A = high from the 1st/2nd mora, B = high from the 3rd–5th mora (unmarked class), C = initial mora high followed by an obligatory fall.
new_statements.secondary_stress: None stated; feet are rhythmic units (iambic lengthening, aspiration foot-initial) but carry no stress.
new_statements.exceptions: fn. 9: 'This account is simplified. There are words with no accent, due to other factors. Unaccented words are pronounced with a High tone on the ultimate mora.' Ogawa 2012 and Lawrence 2013 note east/west Nakijin village pitch differences and variability in where the fall occurs; Lawrence (fall = accent) and Ogawa (rise = accent) disagree on which pitch event is contrastive.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (lexical accent on simple words, cyclic assignment in compounds); Lawrence 2011 p.113 line refers to forms 'cited in isolation'; Nagano-Madsen 2014 shows phrase-level downstep across successive accents.
new_statements.identity_note: Every descriptive source found (both Glottolog refs and all downloaded papers) describes the Nakijin dialect, specifically the Yonamine (与那嶺) community of Nakijin-son on the Motobu peninsula, northern Okinawa Island. Glottolog places this under kuni1268 (Kunigami; sole dialect child Nago, nago1243); Pellard 2015 and Carlino 2022 doubt that 'Kunigami' is a valid subgroup and treat northern-Okinawan varieties as Okinawan. The statement therefore holds for Nakijin-Yonamine, not necessarily for Kunigami-son, Ie, Iheya or other northern-Okinawan dialects (Iheya has its own 2022/2026 chapters by Carlino).

tone_statements.citation: Carlino, Salvatore. 2022. Iheya (Okinawa, Northern Ryukyuan). In Michinori Shimoji (ed.), An Introduction to the Japonic Languages: Grammatical Sketches of Japanese Dialects and Ryukyuan Languages, 58–90. Leiden: Brill. doi:10.1163/9789004519107_004
tone_statements.quote: Iheya is a pitch-accent language. The position of a high pitch within the word is lexically determined and it is distinctive, as in /kii/ (HH) ‘hair’ vs /kii/ (LH) ‘tree’. There are two to three different patterns for accent realization for nominals and two each for verbs and adjectives. … These patterns will be called A, B and C … Type-A nouns have a high pitch assigned from the word-initial mora … Type-B nouns have a high pitch on the final mora … With type-C nouns, the high tone is assigned to the final mora of the noun, but it does not move
tone_statements.locator: pp. 62-63, §2.4 Word-Level Prosody (TBU sentence in §2.2, p. 62; fn. 4 p. 62)
tone_statements.summary: Iheya dialect: lexical pitch accent, the place of the high pitch in the word is distinctive; three accent classes (A, B, C) for longer nouns, two for monosyllables, verbs, adjectives; mora bears tone.

tone_statements.citation: Nagano-Madsen, Yasuko. 2018. Pitch accent typology and intonation in the three dialects of Ryukyuan. Proceedings of Speech Prosody 2018 (Poznań), 734–738. doi:10.21437/SpeechProsody.2018-149
tone_statements.quote: The three dialects of Ryukyuan differ in their lexical pitch accent types; they have an H*L accent (Shuri), an L*H accent (Nakijin), and no accent (Miyako) respectively.
tone_statements.summary: Nakijin: lexical L*H (rising-kernel) pitch accent + phrasal H-/L- tones.

tone_statements.citation: Nagano-Madsen, Yasuko. 2016. Lexical H*+L pitch accent in Ryukyuan: Diversities in phonological patterning and phonetic manifestation. Proceedings of Speech Prosody 2016 (Boston), 455–458. doi:10.21437/SpeechProsody.2016-93
tone_statements.quote: The results showed that Shuri and Nakijin dialects have two entirely different types of F0 manifestation for their H*+L accent regarding the timing of F0 and accented mora, pitch range, and the behavior of post-accent Ls. Furthermore, both the occurrence and distribution of the H*+L accent in Nakijin are limited while it is not in Shuri dialect.
tone_statements.summary: Nakijin: lexical pitch accent; H*+L (falling) accent marginal/restricted in distribution.

tone_statements.citation: Kodama, Nozomi 児玉望. 2014. 名護方言の二つの音声資料の韻律分析 [Prosodic analysis of two sound recordings of the Nago dialect]. ありあけ 熊本大学言語学論集 13: 21–56. Kumamoto: 熊本大学文学部言語学研究室. hdl:2298/29909
tone_statements.quote: この研究ノートは、NHK 資料の全体の、有意味と考えられるピッチ変化に転記を施した上で、間投詞や助詞類を除く各語形のアクセント型を同定する試みである。
tone_statements.translation: This research note is an attempt to transcribe the pitch movements judged meaningful across the whole of the NHK material and then to identify the accent type of every word form, excluding interjections and particles.
tone_statements.summary: Word-accent types identified from pitch transcription of recordings (inventory not in abstract).

tone_statements.citation: Ogawa, Shinji 小川晋史. 2010. 大宜味村津波方言のアクセント体系 [The accent system of the Tsuha dialect, Ogimi village]. 琉球の方言 (Ryukyu no Hogen) 34: 125–174. Tokyo: 法政大学沖縄文化研究所. doi:10.15002/00012520
tone_statements.quote: この調査結果から得られた結論から先に述べると、単純語については音韻的に次のような２型体系であると考えられる。名詞・動詞・形容詞のいずれにおいても同じである。 … この方言の体系内においては語中におけるピッチ上昇の有無によって２種類のアクセント型（ i.e. 高平調と上昇調）が区別できるので、「２～３モーラ語は語末モーラが、４モーラ以上の語では語末から２モーラ目から高くなる」という定義であってもアクセント型を弁別する上で全く問題は生じず、体系として成立する。 … 津波方言は田嘉里方言とは異なり、２型の体系であることがわかった。
tone_statements.translation: To state the conclusion from these survey results first: for simplex words the system is, phonologically, the following two-pattern system. It is the same for nouns, verbs and adjectives. … Within this dialect's system two accent types (i.e. high-level and rising) can be distinguished by whether or not pitch rises within the word, so even a definition like 'in 2-3-mora words the final mora, in words of 4 or more moras the second mora from the end, becomes high' causes no problem at all in telling the accent types apart, and it holds as a system. … The Tsuha dialect, unlike the Tagari dialect, proved to have a two-pattern system.
tone_statements.locator: p. 126 and p. 127, §3.2 単純語のアクセント, last sentence from p. 134, §4 結論と残された問題
tone_statements.summary: Tsuha (Ogimi) has a two-pattern word accent: every simplex word is high-level or rising (final mora high in 2-3-mora words, rise at the penult mora in longer words); compounds follow the first member.

tone_statements.citation: Matsumori, Akiko 松森晶子. 2009. 沖縄本島金武方言の体言のアクセント型とその系列：「琉球調査用系列別語彙」の開発に向けて [Accent classification for nouns in the Kin dialect of mainland Okinawa Island: a step towards a development of word lists for Ryukyuan accent research]. 日本女子大学紀要 文学部 58: 97–122 (paginated (122)–(97)).
tone_statements.quote: 本方言のアクセントの弁別的特徴は、ピッチの「上昇」の位置であると思われる。（すなわち、この方言は上げ核を持つ体系である可能性がある。） … （７）金武方言のアクセント規則 ａ．核の置かれた次モーラを上昇させる。 ｂ．Ａ系列の語は、語頭から３つめのモーラまで高さを持続し、その次のモーラでピッチを下降させる。 … したがって下降の位置は、（少なくとも今のところ）この方言の弁別的な特徴とは言えない11）。 … すなわち、金武方言は「上げ核」の３型体系を持ち、「Ａ系列」は無核（０）、「Ｂ系列」は語末モーラ核（−１）、「Ｃ系列」は語末から数えて２つ目のモーラに核がある（−２）、というような体系を持つと記述される。
tone_statements.translation: The distinctive feature of this dialect's accent seems to be the position of the pitch 'rise' (i.e. it may be a system with a rising kernel). … (7) Kin dialect accent rules: a. Raise the mora after the one bearing the kernel. b. A-series words keep high pitch up to the third mora from the start and lower it on the next mora. … So the position of the fall cannot (at least for now) be called a distinctive feature of this dialect. … That is, the Kin dialect is described as a three-pattern 'rising-kernel' system: A series kernel-less (0), B series kernel on the word-final mora (−1), C series kernel on the second mora from the end (−2).
tone_statements.locator: pp. 107–109, §3 金武方言のアクセント体系と系列: opening + (7) on p. 107, fall remark on p. 108, summary after (10) on p. 109
tone_statements.summary: Kin dialect nouns: pitch accent with a rising kernel, three classes (unaccented; kernel on final mora; kernel on penult); mora after the kernel is raised; fall not distinctive; stress not discussed.

tone_statements.citation: Oshio, Mutsuko 生塩睦子. 1985. 沖縄伊江島方言の語アクセント [Word accent of the Ie-jima dialect, Okinawa]. 沖縄文化研究 11: 17–94. Tokyo: 法政大学沖縄文化研究所. doi:10.15002/00002714
tone_statements.quote: 伊江島方言のアクセントは，下がり目すなわち下り核がどこにあるか，でとらえるのが妥当であろう。当方言アクセントの音韻的型は，次の６つのタイプに分けることができる。 … i 平板型（核をもたない） … ii 尾高Ⅰ型（最終音節に核がある） … iii 尾高Ⅱ型（後から２番目の音節に核がある） … iv 中高型（第１・２音節及び後から１・２番目の音節，以外の音節に核がある） … v 頭高Ⅱ型 … vi 頭高Ⅰ型 … 名詞のアクセント型の種類は，《音節数＋１》個あるが，各アクセント型の所属語彙に著しい片よりがみられる。
tone_statements.translation: The accent of the Ie-jima dialect is best captured by where the fall, i.e. the lowering kernel, lies. The phonological accent patterns of this dialect can be divided into the following six types. … i level type (no kernel) … ii final-high type I (kernel on the last syllable) … iii final-high type II (kernel on the second syllable from the end) … iv mid-high type (kernel on a syllable other than the first two and the last two) … v initial-high type II … vi initial-high type I … The number of accent-pattern types for nouns is (number of syllables + 1), but the vocabulary belonging to each type is markedly skewed.
tone_statements.locator: p. 20, §2 伊江島方言アクセントの概観 and p. 23, §3 名詞のアクセント first sentence; supporting p. 18
tone_statements.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone_statements.summary: Word pitch accent: a word is unaccented or has one lexically fixed pitch fall (lowering kernel) whose position contrasts; six positional types, n+1 patterns for n-unit nouns; rise non-distinctive.

tone_statements.citation: Kusakabe, Fumio 日下部文夫. 1968. 沖縄北部方言アクセント調査語彙について [On the word-list for the survey on the accentuation in the northern area of Okinawa Archipelago]. 言語研究 (Gengo Kenkyu) 52: 33–57. doi:10.11435/gengo1939.1968.33
tone_statements.quote: According to the usual segmental way of putting toneme on one mora (or on the short syllable) … But, by adapting the idea of one (ascending or descending or prolonging) toneme on the long syllable, we can identify it with the short syllable. One syllable has one seat for the toneme regardless of its quantity. The word-list for the survey on the accentuation in the area should be arranged by the following scheme of the bisyllabics providing twelve classes of accentual types …
tone_statements.locator: English summary, p. 56; cf. sec. 3.2 p. 40 and sec. 0.2 p. 34
tone_statements.summary: Word pitch accent of the Japanese-Ryukyuan kind: nouns fall into accent types with high-level, rising or falling shapes; one toneme per syllable, a long syllable taking a rising, falling or long one.

sources.citation: Lawrence, Wayne P. (2017). 今帰仁方言の用言アクセントの起源について. 琉球の方言 41: 1–23. doi:10.15002/00014494
sources.note: p.1: the Yonamine/Nakijin dialect is unusual among Ryukyuan in having an accent in addition to tone (Lawrence 1990, 2001); the accent blocks lengthening of adjacent high vowels; H tone goes to the last accent and to the mora after the initial foot; verbs: accent on the pre-final mora of the ending /-iuN/, position predictable from word structure.

sources.citation: Nagano-Madsen, Yasuko 永野マドセン泰子 (2014). 今帰仁方言アクセントの音声分析. 琉球の方言 38: 51–67. doi:10.15002/00012496
sources.note: §2 pp.51–52: Ryukyuan accent types are (i) falling-kernel (Shuri, fixed on the 2nd mora), (ii) rising-kernel where the place of the pitch rise is distinctive, exemplified by Nakijin, (iii) accentless (Irabu); repeats Ogawa's three types; F0 study shows the Nakijin HL 'falling' type differs from Tokyo-type falls and that sequences of rising accents use downstep.

sources.citation: Lawrence, Wayne P. (2013). [Book Review] Ogawa Shinji (2012) Nakijin-hōgen-akusento-no shosō. International Journal of Okinawan Studies 4(1): 141–147. hdl:20.500.12000/35906
sources.note: p.141: Nakasone 1983 (Yonamine dialect) underlies three PhDs (Lawrence 1990, Curry 2004, Ogawa 2009); pp.142–144: Lawrence treats the accent as the (potential) locus of a fall, Ogawa the locus of the rise; both agree the accent blocks Rhythmic (iambic) Lengthening of adjacent high vowels.

sources.citation: Ogawa, Shinji 小川晋史 (2012). 〈受賞紹介〉今帰仁方言のアクセント体系. NINJAL Project Review 7: 41–43. doi:10.15084/00000694 (summary of his 2009 Kobe University PhD)
sources.note: p.41 (1) 今帰仁方言の3型アクセント: A型 = high pitch from the 1st or 2nd mora; B型 = high pitch from the 3rd–5th mora; C型 = word-initial mora high with an obligatory fall right after; B is the unmarked, C the most marked type; the prosodic unit is the mora and the contrastive element is the rise (昇り核); foot structure is essential (Rhythmic Lengthening).

sources.citation: Ogawa, Shinji 小川晋史. 2010. 大宜味村津波方言のアクセント体系 [The accent system of the Tsuha dialect, Ogimi village]. 琉球の方言 (Ryukyu no Hogen) 34: 125–174. Tokyo: 法政大学沖縄文化研究所. doi:10.15002/00012520
sources.quote: この調査結果から得られた結論から先に述べると、単純語については音韻的に次のような２型体系であると考えられる。名詞・動詞・形容詞のいずれにおいても同じである。 … この方言の体系内においては語中におけるピッチ上昇の有無によって２種類のアクセント型（ i.e. 高平調と上昇調）が区別できるので、「２～３モーラ語は語末モーラが、４モーラ以上の語では語末から２モーラ目から高くなる」という定義であってもアクセント型を弁別する上で全く問題は生じず、体系として成立する。 … 津波方言は田嘉里方言とは異なり、２型の体系であることがわかった。
sources.locator: p. 126 and p. 127, §3.2 単純語のアクセント, last sentence from p. 134, §4 結論と残された問題
sources.note: Describes another variety. Tsuha (Ogimi) has a two-pattern word accent: every simplex word is high-level or rising (final mora high in 2-3-mora words, rise at the penult mora in longer words); compounds follow the first member.

tone.quote: この調査結果から得られた結論から先に述べると、単純語については音韻的に次のような２型体系であると考えられる。名詞・動詞・形容詞のいずれにおいても同じである。 … この方言の体系内においては語中におけるピッチ上昇の有無によって２種類のアクセント型（ i.e. 高平調と上昇調）が区別できるので、「２～３モーラ語は語末モーラが、４モーラ以上の語では語末から２モーラ目から高くなる」という定義であってもアクセント型を弁別する上で全く問題は生じず、体系として成立する。 … 津波方言は田嘉里方言とは異なり、２型の体系であることがわかった。
tone.locator: p. 126 and p. 127, §3.2 単純語のアクセント, last sentence from p. 134, §4 結論と残された問題
tone.translation: To state the conclusion from these survey results first: for simplex words the system is, phonologically, the following two-pattern system. It is the same for nouns, verbs and adjectives. … Within this dialect's system two accent types (i.e. high-level and rising) can be distinguished by whether or not pitch rises within the word, so even a definition like 'in 2-3-mora words the final mora, in words of 4 or more moras the second mora from the end, becomes high' causes no problem at all in telling the accent types apart, and it holds as a system. … The Tsuha dialect, unlike the Tagari dialect, proved to have a two-pattern system.
tone.summary: Tsuha (Ogimi) has a two-pattern word accent: every simplex word is high-level or rising (final mora high in 2-3-mora words, rise at the penult mora in longer words); compounds follow the first member.

sources.citation: Matsumori, Akiko 松森晶子. 2009. 沖縄本島金武方言の体言のアクセント型とその系列：「琉球調査用系列別語彙」の開発に向けて [Accent classification for nouns in the Kin dialect of mainland Okinawa Island: a step towards a development of word lists for Ryukyuan accent research]. 日本女子大学紀要 文学部 58: 97–122 (paginated (122)–(97)).
sources.quote: 本方言のアクセントの弁別的特徴は、ピッチの「上昇」の位置であると思われる。（すなわち、この方言は上げ核を持つ体系である可能性がある。） … （７）金武方言のアクセント規則 ａ．核の置かれた次モーラを上昇させる。 ｂ．Ａ系列の語は、語頭から３つめのモーラまで高さを持続し、その次のモーラでピッチを下降させる。 … したがって下降の位置は、（少なくとも今のところ）この方言の弁別的な特徴とは言えない11）。 … すなわち、金武方言は「上げ核」の３型体系を持ち、「Ａ系列」は無核（０）、「Ｂ系列」は語末モーラ核（−１）、「Ｃ系列」は語末から数えて２つ目のモーラに核がある（−２）、というような体系を持つと記述される。
sources.locator: pp. 107–109, §3 金武方言のアクセント体系と系列: opening + (7) on p. 107, fall remark on p. 108, summary after (10) on p. 109
sources.note: Describes another variety. Kin dialect nouns: pitch accent with a rising kernel, three classes (unaccented; kernel on final mora; kernel on penult); mora after the kernel is raised; fall not distinctive; stress not discussed.
sources.venue: 日本女子大学紀要 文学部

tone.quote: 本方言のアクセントの弁別的特徴は、ピッチの「上昇」の位置であると思われる。（すなわち、この方言は上げ核を持つ体系である可能性がある。） … （７）金武方言のアクセント規則 ａ．核の置かれた次モーラを上昇させる。 ｂ．Ａ系列の語は、語頭から３つめのモーラまで高さを持続し、その次のモーラでピッチを下降させる。 … したがって下降の位置は、（少なくとも今のところ）この方言の弁別的な特徴とは言えない11）。 … すなわち、金武方言は「上げ核」の３型体系を持ち、「Ａ系列」は無核（０）、「Ｂ系列」は語末モーラ核（−１）、「Ｃ系列」は語末から数えて２つ目のモーラに核がある（−２）、というような体系を持つと記述される。
tone.locator: pp. 107–109, §3 金武方言のアクセント体系と系列: opening + (7) on p. 107, fall remark on p. 108, summary after (10) on p. 109
tone.translation: The distinctive feature of this dialect's accent seems to be the position of the pitch 'rise' (i.e. it may be a system with a rising kernel). … (7) Kin dialect accent rules: a. Raise the mora after the one bearing the kernel. b. A-series words keep high pitch up to the third mora from the start and lower it on the next mora. … So the position of the fall cannot (at least for now) be called a distinctive feature of this dialect. … That is, the Kin dialect is described as a three-pattern 'rising-kernel' system: A series kernel-less (0), B series kernel on the word-final mora (−1), C series kernel on the second mora from the end (−2).
tone.summary: Kin dialect nouns: pitch accent with a rising kernel, three classes (unaccented; kernel on final mora; kernel on penult); mora after the kernel is raised; fall not distinctive; stress not discussed.
tone.says: Kin dialect nouns: pitch accent with a rising kernel, three classes (unaccented; kernel on final mora; kernel on penult); mora after the kernel is raised; fall not distinctive; stress not discussed.

sources.citation: Oshio, Mutsuko 生塩睦子. 1985. 沖縄伊江島方言の語アクセント [Word accent of the Ie-jima dialect, Okinawa]. 沖縄文化研究 11: 17–94. Tokyo: 法政大学沖縄文化研究所. doi:10.15002/00002714
sources.quote: 伊江島方言のアクセントは，下がり目すなわち下り核がどこにあるか，でとらえるのが妥当であろう。当方言アクセントの音韻的型は，次の６つのタイプに分けることができる。 … i 平板型（核をもたない） … ii 尾高Ⅰ型（最終音節に核がある） … iii 尾高Ⅱ型（後から２番目の音節に核がある） … iv 中高型（第１・２音節及び後から１・２番目の音節，以外の音節に核がある） … v 頭高Ⅱ型 … vi 頭高Ⅰ型 … 名詞のアクセント型の種類は，《音節数＋１》個あるが，各アクセント型の所属語彙に著しい片よりがみられる。
sources.locator: p. 20, §2 伊江島方言アクセントの概観 and p. 23, §3 名詞のアクセント first sentence; supporting p. 18
sources.note: Describes another variety. Word pitch accent: a word is unaccented or has one lexically fixed pitch fall (lowering kernel) whose position contrasts; six positional types, n+1 patterns for n-unit nouns; rise non-distinctive.

tone.quote: 伊江島方言のアクセントは，下がり目すなわち下り核がどこにあるか，でとらえるのが妥当であろう。当方言アクセントの音韻的型は，次の６つのタイプに分けることができる。 … i 平板型（核をもたない） … ii 尾高Ⅰ型（最終音節に核がある） … iii 尾高Ⅱ型（後から２番目の音節に核がある） … iv 中高型（第１・２音節及び後から１・２番目の音節，以外の音節に核がある） … v 頭高Ⅱ型 … vi 頭高Ⅰ型 … 名詞のアクセント型の種類は，《音節数＋１》個あるが，各アクセント型の所属語彙に著しい片よりがみられる。
tone.locator: p. 20, §2 伊江島方言アクセントの概観 and p. 23, §3 名詞のアクセント first sentence; supporting p. 18
tone.translation: The accent of the Ie-jima dialect is best captured by where the fall, i.e. the lowering kernel, lies. The phonological accent patterns of this dialect can be divided into the following six types. … i level type (no kernel) … ii final-high type I (kernel on the last syllable) … iii final-high type II (kernel on the second syllable from the end) … iv mid-high type (kernel on a syllable other than the first two and the last two) … v initial-high type II … vi initial-high type I … The number of accent-pattern types for nouns is (number of syllables + 1), but the vocabulary belonging to each type is markedly skewed.
tone.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
tone.summary: Word pitch accent: a word is unaccented or has one lexically fixed pitch fall (lowering kernel) whose position contrasts; six positional types, n+1 patterns for n-unit nouns; rise non-distinctive.
tone.says: Word pitch accent: a word is unaccented or has one lexically fixed pitch fall (lowering kernel) whose position contrasts; six positional types, n+1 patterns for n-unit nouns; rise non-distinctive.

sources.quote: According to the usual segmental way of putting toneme on one mora (or on the short syllable) … But, by adapting the idea of one (ascending or descending or prolonging) toneme on the long syllable, we can identify it with the short syllable. One syllable has one seat for the toneme regardless of its quantity. The word-list for the survey on the accentuation in the area should be arranged by the following scheme of the bisyllabics providing twelve classes of accentual types …

(Companion: Matsumori 2024, 沖縄語金武方言のアクセント型別語彙集(名詞篇), 日本女子大学大学院文学研究科紀要.)

sources.venue: 日本女子大学紀要 文学部

tone.quote: 以下、金武方言の３種のアクセント型をａ型，ｂ型，ｃ型と呼ぶ9）。 … 金武方言のａ型は、名詞を含む文節のピッチが高く開始し、原則的にその文節内の頭から数えて３モーラ目直後にピッチの急激な下降が出現する10）。 … このｂ型の最大の特徴は、その型を持つ語から開始する文節内部に、かならず重起伏音調が出現するという点にある。 … ｃ型は、次に見られるように語末、あるいは語末モーラの直後のモーラを、原則的に１モーラ分だけ上昇させる。 … 金武方言の複合語の韻律型は、原則的にその前部要素によって決定する。
tone.translation: Below, the three accent types of the Kin dialect are called a-type, b-type and c-type. … In the Kin a-type the phrase containing the noun starts high and, in principle, a sharp pitch fall appears right after the 3rd mora counted from the start of that phrase. … The chief trait of the b-type is that a double-peaked contour always appears inside a phrase beginning with a word of that type. … The c-type, as seen below, in principle raises the word-final mora, or the mora right after it, by just one mora's length. … The prosodic type of a Kin compound is in principle determined by its first member.
tone.summary: Kin dialect (central Okinawa I.), not Nakijin: nouns take one of three accent patterns (a: high onset, fall after 3rd mora; b: double peak; c: final-mora rise); compounds follow the first member.

sources.citation: Carlino, Salvatore. 2020. 北琉球沖縄語伊平屋方言の文法 [A grammar of the Iheya dialect of Okinawan, Northern Ryukyuan]. PhD dissertation (博士(学術), 甲第1094号), 一橋大学 Hitotsubashi University. doi:10.15057/31184, hdl:10086/31184
sources.note: Describes another variety. Iheya dialect: three-pattern pitch accent (noun types A, B, C) marked by presence and position of a pitch rise; the mora bears the rise; pitch fall not distinctive; verbs/adjectives have only A and B.

tone.quote: 伊平屋方言はいわゆる 3 型アクセント体系を持っている。 … 伊平屋方言の 3 つのアクセント型は、ピッチの上昇の有無と位置で区別される。ピッチ上昇を担う単位はモーラである。1 音節の名詞には A 型と B 型しかない。2 音節以上の名詞には A 型、B 型、C 型がある。アクセント型 A の名詞では語頭から高く発音される。B 型は文節を領域として上昇位置が決定され、、上昇は文節末モーラに現れるが、 … C 型の名詞では（分節ではなく）語を領域として上昇位置が決定され、いかなる環境でも語末モーラにピッチの上昇が起きる。
tone.locator: §2.7.1 アクセント概要, p. 53 and §2.7.1.7 まとめ, p. 62
tone.translation: The Iheya dialect has a so-called three-pattern accent system. … The three accent types of Iheya are distinguished by the presence and position of a pitch rise. The unit that bears the rise is the mora. One-syllable nouns have only types A and B; nouns of two or more syllables have A, B and C. Type-A nouns are high from the start of the word. For type B the rise position is set over the bunsetsu (word + clitics) and the rise appears on the bunsetsu-final mora, … for type-C nouns it is set over the word (not the bunsetsu), and the pitch rise occurs on the word-final mora in every environment.
tone.summary: Iheya dialect: three-pattern pitch accent (noun types A, B, C) marked by presence and position of a pitch rise; the mora bears the rise; pitch fall not distinctive; verbs/adjectives have only A and B.
tone.says: Iheya dialect: three-pattern pitch accent (noun types A, B, C) marked by presence and position of a pitch rise; the mora bears the rise; pitch fall not distinctive; verbs/adjectives have only A and B.
